logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, changing a wiki (repository documentation) page title through Edit resets the page's visible Revisions list to the rename commit, even though the wiki commit itself identifies a file rename with an existing parent history. Users cannot review the page's earlier content revisions from the renamed page.

rootCause.explanation: renderRevisionPage queries FileCommitsCount and CommitsByFileAndRange using only the current filename. It does not follow renames to the previous filename, hiding earlier revisions.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, changing a wiki page title through Edit resets the page's visible Revisions list to the rename commit, even though the wiki commit itself identifies a file rename with an existing parent history. Users cannot review the page's earlier content revisions from the renamed page.

sourceBugs.name: Renaming a wiki page hides its earlier revisions from page history

reproductionPaths.expected: A renamed wiki page retains its earlier creation and edit revisions in the page's Revisions view, so its content history remains accessible.
reproductionPaths.actual: In eval/D-from-template, D-history-1 showed 2 revisions after creation and a content edit. Renaming it to D-history-2 preserved content but reduced the Revisions view to 1 commit, 'D- rename history'. A later edit raised it to only 2 commits (rename plus later edit), still omitting both pre-rename revisions. The rename commit detail shows D-history-1.-.md → D-history-2.-.md with a parent commit, confirming the earlier Git history exists. The old page URL redirects to Pages.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a repository’s Wiki.
Create a page named History-before with first content.
Edit its content without changing its title and save. Verify the page has two revisions.
Edit again, changing only the title to History-after, and save.
Open the renamed page’s Revisions. Observe only the rename commit appears, omitting the two earlier revisions even though the rename commit has a parent and records the filename change.

logicalBugs.explanation: A Gitea wiki is a repository’s documentation area, and its Revisions list can open a revision’s change comparison. At phone width the revision rows provide no visible way to open that comparison, although the same revision links are available and work on desktop.

rootCause.explanation: Wiki history reuses commits_list where the SHA cell links to /wiki/commit. The mobile .commit-table td.sha rule hides that cell, and the wiki branch omits the alternative view-at-revision action.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A Gitea wiki is a repository’s documentation area, and its Revisions list can open a revision’s change comparison. At phone width the revision rows provide no visible way to open that comparison, although the same revision links are available and work on desktop.

sourceBugs.name: Mobile wiki history provides no visible navigation to revision diffs

reproductionPaths.expected: The narrow-screen wiki history UI exposes a visible way to open a listed revision’s diff. It need not retain the SHA column or make the message text clickable if another normal UI control provides that navigation.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390×844 the SHA column and its revision-diff links are hidden. Revision messages are plain text, and the remaining copy-hash control does not open a diff. No alternative diff-navigation control is provided in the history UI. At 1440×1000 the same revision’s SHA link opens the diff viewer.
reproSteps: Sign in with wiki write access to an unarchived repository and create a disposable wiki page with initial content.
Edit that page with distinct content, supply a unique plain-text commit note, and save, producing at least two revisions.
Use the page’s revision-history control to open its Revisions view and set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Inspect the visible revision navigation. The SHA links are hidden, the commit-note text is not linked, and the copy-hash control offers no navigation to the diff viewer.

For comparison, view the same history at 1440×1000 and click a revision’s SHA link. It opens that wiki revision’s diff. The failure being graded is the absent mobile UI route to this working viewer, not omission of a particular column.

logicalBugs.explanation: Gitea’s wiki (repository documentation) rejects duplicate titles during page creation but fails to check them when renaming. Saving a renamed page replaces another page's content without warning and removes the source page.

rootCause.explanation: updateWikiPage rejects existing destination paths only in isNew mode. Edit mode removes the old path and adds the submitted content at the destination even when that destination already exists.

reproductionPaths.explanation: Gitea’s wiki rejects duplicate titles during page creation but fails to check them when renaming. Saving a renamed page replaces another page's content without warning and removes the source page.

sourceBugs.name: Renaming a wiki page to an existing title silently overwrites the target

reproductionPaths.actual: Renaming Rename Source to Rename Target saves successfully. Rename Target now displays Source content marker QA instead of Target content marker QA, persists after reload, and the original Rename Source is removed. Also reproduced by renaming Folder/Page to existing Café guide.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open /qa-org-20261009/qa-template-copy/wiki (or another editable repository wiki).
Create Rename Source with content Source content marker QA.
Create Rename Target with content Target content marker QA.
Edit Rename Source, change only Page title to Rename Target, and click Save Page.
Observe there is no duplicate-title error or overwrite confirmation. Rename Target now contains Source content marker QA.
Reload Rename Target and open the original Rename Source URL to verify the overwritten content persists and the source page no longer exists.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, in a hosted wiki, relative links to other documentation pages work after saving, but Preview can turn them into absolute links using an internal localhost host forwarded by the deployment proxy. Clicking a preview link then leaves the reachable application and fails. This requires that host/proxy configuration and is not a claim that every relative wiki link or every deployment is broken.

rootCause.explanation: Wiki preview Markup mode enables WithUseAbsoluteLink(true). RepoWiki.ResolveLink resolves page links relative to repoLink/wiki through its RenderContext, whose absolute-link path invokes httplib.MakeAbsoluteURL. GuessCurrentHostURL combines the forwarded/request scheme with req.Host; when the proxy forwards the internal localhost:5503 Host, preview links become https://localhost:5503/... while saved-page relative links stay on the browser host. This depends on the proxy/request-header prerequisite preserved in the original matchingGuidance; it is not evidence that an arbitrary configured ROOT_URL is always used.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, on a hosted wiki with the proxy forwarding an internal localhost host, preview a relative link to another wiki page. Preview turns it into an unreachable internal-host URL, although the same link works from the saved page, so this path depends on that deployment header configuration.

sourceBugs.name: Wiki preview links point to localhost and fail to open existing pages

reproductionPaths.expected: Preview links to another wiki page should open that page on the current application host, as they do on the saved page.
reproductionPaths.actual: The preview's Second page link is https://localhost:5503/admin/harbor-handbook/wiki/Second-Page. Clicking it opens a browser error: localhost refused to connect, ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open /admin/harbor-handbook/wiki.
Create a page named Second Page and save it with any content.
Create or edit Home with the Markdown link [Second page](Second-Page) and save. The saved link uses /admin/harbor-handbook/wiki/Second-Page.
Edit Home and select Preview.
Click Second page in the preview; observe the localhost connection failure.

guidance.acceptanceScope: Accepted as a valid reference by user instruction; source prerequisites and remaining evidence gaps are retained below.
prerequisites: Preview request backend Host is localhost:5503 and forwarded scheme is https (or an equivalent incorrect guessed application origin).

rootCause.explanation: new.tmpl assigns the welcome text whenever PageIsWikiEdit is false, even on a POST rerender with submitted .content. Duplicate-name and whitespace-title validation preserve the form data server-side but the template overwrites its body.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, on narrow wiki (repository documentation) pages, a long page title makes the closed Page selector extend beyond the viewport and can cover the adjacent Code button. The selector retains the full title width instead of truncating it, introducing horizontal scrolling that pushes article content and actions out of view.

rootCause.explanation: The wiki header renders its title within a flex dropdown trigger beside action controls without a narrow-width truncation constraint. Long title text retains its width and overlaps the Code control.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, at a 320px width, a long wiki-page title covers the Code button and intercepts normal clicks.

sourceBugs.name: Long wiki title covers the mobile Code button

reproductionPaths.expected: At 320px, selecting a valid wiki page must keep the Code dropdown visible and usable without the title painting over it. Wrapping controls or truncating the displayed title is acceptable.
reproductionPaths.actual: On Home, Page: Home and the blue Code dropdown were separately visible. After selecting CaseNarrowNav-7314 Δ Momentic2026, the page chooser stretched across the row and the Code dropdown was no longer visible. This remained the rendered state after a six-second wait.
reproSteps: Sign in with wiki-write permission, set the viewport to 320 by 800 CSS pixels, and open the repository Wiki through its tab.
Choose New Page, use a unique title of similar length to CaseNarrowNav-7314 Δ Momentic2026, keep nonempty content, and save.
Use the Page chooser to select Home. Confirm the chooser and Code control are separately visible.
Open the Page chooser, filter for the unique title, and select that page.
After the row settles, observe that the title stretches across the row and covers the adjacent Code control.

It runs past the right edge with its dropdown arrow off screen, and scrolling sideways to reach it pushes the article and the Edit/New/Delete buttons off the left side.

reproductionPaths.expected: The closed Page selector fits the mobile viewport, truncating the title the way the page heading does, with its arrow visible.

Scrolling right showed the selector's arrow but moved the article and the Edit/New/Delete buttons off the left side. The page heading below it was truncated with an ellipsis.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, when a wiki (repository documentation) body has unsaved edits in the legacy editor, navigating to the repository Wiki page list proceeds without a warning and silently discards the changes. The simple editor presents a dismissible navigation confirmation for the same action.

rootCause.explanation: Dirty detection listens to input/change events on named form controls. EasyMDE updates the hidden textarea through forceSync and emits only a custom editor-content event from its CodeMirror change callback; it does not emit the textarea input event that the form dirty tracker requires.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, when a wiki body has unsaved edits in the legacy editor, navigating to the repository Wiki page list proceeds without a warning and silently discards the changes. The simple editor presents a dismissible navigation confirmation for the same action.

reproductionPaths.actual: After adding a visible marker to the legacy wiki body and blurring the editor, clicking the repository Wiki tab navigates to the page list without a warning. Reopening Edit shows only the saved baseline. With the same navigation in simple textarea mode, the confirmation can be dismissed and the unsaved marker remains in the form.
reproSteps: Create and save a wiki page with a known baseline body, then open Edit and select Use the legacy editor instead.
Append a visible marker to the body and blur through the optional update-note field without saving.
Click the repository Wiki tab. Observe that navigation proceeds without a confirmation.
Reopen Edit and observe that only the saved baseline remains; the unsaved legacy marker was discarded.
Switch to simple textarea mode, append a different marker, blur the body, and click Wiki again. Dismiss the navigation confirmation and observe that the edit form and marker remain.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, edit a wiki (repository documentation) page’s title to a value that normalizes to no filename, such as spaces or a single dot. Save reports success and silently renames the page to unnamed instead of rejecting or explaining the normalized title.

rootCause.explanation: UserTitleToWebPath trims whitespace and normalizes path segments, then substitutes unnamed for an empty result. EditWikiPost lacks the new-page whitespace-title validation and neither create nor edit tells the user when dot-only input normalizes to unnamed.

logicalBugs.explanation: Gitea’s repository wiki (repository documentation) reserves certain page names for routes, including raw. Renaming an existing page to such a reserved name opens a full-page Internal Server Error instead of leaving the editor available with a title-validation message.

rootCause.explanation: updateWikiPage rejects reserved names, but EditWikiPost routes every service error to ServerError. Unlike NewWikiPost, it never handles ErrWikiReservedName by rerendering the draft with a field error.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, create a wiki (repository documentation) page whose literal title contains a hyphen, trailing .md or plus sign, then link to it with [[Title]]. The rendered link does not match the page’s encoded storage route and opens a different page or the page list.

rootCause.explanation: The wiki-style markup processor substitutes spaces and uses url.PathEscape rather than wiki.UserTitleToWebPath. It never adds the .- marker for literal hyphens or .md suffixes and leaves + unescaped for a server decoder that uses QueryUnescape, so valid titles resolve as different pages.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, saving a wiki (repository documentation) editor opened before another user/tab changed the page silently writes its stale contents. It can overwrite a newer edit, recreate a deleted page, or recreate the old title after a rename without warning that the page changed while the editor was open.

rootCause.explanation: The web form submits title/content/message but no starting commit or blob ID. updateWikiPage reads the current HEAD and writes submitted content without comparing it with the revision opened by the editor, overwriting newer content or recreating an old/deleted path.

reproductionPaths.explanation: The wiki editor carries no record of the revision it was opened from, so saving an editor opened before another save replaces the page with the older body. The newer saved change disappears without warning, unlike Gitea's file editor and issue editor, which reject the same stale save.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor silently discards newer edits

reproductionPaths.expected: When the page changed after the editor was opened, the save is refused with a conflict message (as the repository file editor and issue description editor do) or the edits are merged, and the newer saved change is kept.
reproductionPaths.actual: Two editors are opened on a checklist page with 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'. The second editor adds 'Check radio' and saves. The first, now stale, changes only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and saves successfully with no warning. The page now lists 'Check ropes carefully' and 'Check tide'; 'Check radio' is gone, and the new revision's diff deletes it. Reload confirms the loss. The same happens across two users.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with a checklist containing 'Check ropes' and 'Check tide'.
Open that page's Edit form in two tabs before saving either.
In the second tab, append 'Check radio' and click Save Page.
In the first tab, change only 'Check ropes' to 'Check ropes carefully' and click Save Page.
Reload the page and observe 'Check radio' is gone, with no warning shown at save time.

reproductionPaths.expected: A stale edit to a page that was renamed elsewhere is rejected with a conflict warning or applied to the renamed page; it doesn't create a second page at the old title.
reproductionPaths.actual: The stale save succeeded with no warning and created a page at the old title holding the stale edit. The renamed page kept its earlier content, and the page list showed both titles.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page and open its editor in tab A without saving.
In tab B, edit the same page, change only its title, and save.
In tab A, change only the body and save.
Check the wiki page list and the contents of both titles.

sourceBugs.name: Saving a stale wiki editor after the page was deleted silently recreates it

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, at phone width, opening a wiki's Page picker when one page has a long title sizes the menu to that title with no width cap. The menu runs off the right edge and the whole page scrolls sideways, clipping the wiki's left edge.

rootCause.explanation: The floating filter dropdown renders every full page title as an item and allows content-driven menu width. A single long title therefore widens the menu beyond phone width and increases horizontal scroll area.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, at phone width, opening a wiki's Page picker when one page has a long title sizes the menu to that title with no width cap. The menu runs off the right edge and the whole page scrolls sideways, clipping the wiki's left edge.

sourceBugs.name: Long wiki page title makes the open mobile Page picker overflow and shift the page

reproductionPaths.expected: At phone width the open Page picker fits the screen, wrapping or truncating long page names, and the rest of the wiki stays in place.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390×844 with a 73-character page title, the open Page menu was about 530px wide and its filter about 506px. The document grew to about 538px wide and scrolled sideways about 20px, cutting off the logo and the Page button at the left; the menu and long title ran off the right. Filtering and navigation still worked.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page titled 'Harbor operations handbook for onboarding and emergency response procedures'.
At 390×844, open the wiki's Home page.
Tap the 'Page: Home' button to open the page picker and look at both edges of the screen.

relatedReference.distinction: Same long-title trigger. That entry is the closed page/title area covering the mobile Code button; this entry is the open Page picker menu overflowing and shifting the whole page sideways.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea’s standard Markdown toolbar used by wiki (repository documentation) pages and release notes, a heading button inserts # markers at the caret instead of making the current line a heading. Selecting text and changing heading levels can stack prefixes such as "# ## ### Heading" rather than replace the existing level.

rootCause.explanation: The shared combomarkdowneditor template uses markdown-toolbar-element md-header directly. Its selection-prefix operation is not adapted to select the whole current line or normalize an existing heading prefix, so both caret insertion and repeated level changes retain incorrect Markdown.

analysis.explanation: The shared Markdown editor toolbar delegates heading prefix insertion to its selection-based toolbar action, which operates at the caret/selection and does not replace the line existing heading prefix.

The shared toolbar uses markdown-toolbar-element md-header directly. Its prefix operation uses the current selection/caret, and the integration does not expand the selection to the whole line, allowing ## to be inserted after existing text.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In a Gitea wiki page’s standard Markdown editor, place the cursor at the end of an existing text line and click a heading button without selecting the line. The heading marker is appended after the text, leaving ordinary text in Preview instead of converting the line into a heading.

sourceBugs.name: Wiki editor heading button appends ## after the text instead of making a heading

reproductionPaths.expected: Clicking Add heading turns the current line into a heading by putting the ## marker at the start of the line.
reproductionPaths.actual: With 'Toolbar heading' typed and the caret at the end, clicking the H2 button produced 'Toolbar heading## '; Preview and the saved page showed ordinary text, not a heading. It works only with the caret at the start of the line or the line selected; the new issue editor inserts the heading correctly.
reproSteps: Open a repository Wiki and click New Page.
Type 'Toolbar heading' in the content and leave the caret at the end with nothing selected.
Click the heading (H2) toolbar button, then click Preview.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea’s EasyMDE Markdown editor used for wiki (repository documentation) pages and release notes, toolbar tooltips advertise formatting shortcuts such as "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing the shortcut leaves selected text unchanged. Clicking the corresponding Bold or Italic toolbar button works.

rootCause.explanation: switchToEasyMDE replaces CodeMirror extraKeys with a new map containing quick-submit and mention-navigation handlers. This discards EasyMDE formatting key bindings while its toolbar still advertises them. The Ctrl-B tooltip in the release report identifies this EasyMDE path even though that report calls it the enhanced editor; the standard textarea toolbar uses the different "Add bold text" tooltip.

analysis.explanation: The toolbar provides a Bold shortcut tooltip, while the enhanced editor custom key bindings do not install an equivalent bold handler for the textarea mode.

After EasyMDE creates its default keymap, switchToEasyMDE sets extraKeys to a new map containing quick-submit and mention-navigation handlers. It replaces the formatting shortcut bindings while toolbar titles still advertise them.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea’s legacy (EasyMDE) Markdown editor, used after 'Use the legacy editor instead', the toolbar buttons' tooltips advertise shortcuts such as 'Bold (Ctrl-B)' and 'Italic (Ctrl-I)', but pressing them does nothing. The toolbar buttons themselves work.

sourceBugs.name: Legacy editor toolbar advertises keyboard shortcuts that do nothing

reproductionPaths.expected: The advertised shortcuts apply their formatting (for example Ctrl-B makes the selection bold), or the tooltips don't advertise them.
reproductionPaths.actual: In the legacy editor on a wiki page, with text selected, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+I left the text unchanged, while clicking the Bold button produced '**…**'. The buttons' titles read 'Bold (Ctrl-B)', 'Italic (Ctrl-I)', 'Link (Ctrl-K)' and so on.
reproSteps: Open a wiki page editor and click 'Use the legacy editor instead' in the Markdown toolbar.
Type and select some text, then press Ctrl+B.
Hover the Bold button to read its tooltip, then click it on the same selection.

relatedReference.distinction: Both are wiki editor formatting controls. That entry is the heading toolbar button appending ## at the end of the line; this entry is the legacy editor's advertised keyboard shortcuts doing nothing.
Both are wiki editor formatting controls. That entry is the heading toolbar button appending ## at the end of the line; this entry is the legacy editor's advertised keyboard shortcuts doing nothing.

logicalBugs.explanation: A Gitea wiki (repository documentation) _Footer (or other wiki page) whose Markdown starts with '---' renders without the horizontal rule, and its blank-line-separated paragraphs run together on one line. The leading '---' is treated as the start of front matter instead of a rule. Without the leading '---' the same content renders normally.

rootCause.explanation: The Markdown renderer enables goldmark-meta unconditionally. A leading --- is parsed as YAML front matter rather than a horizontal rule; content before a closing delimiter/end is consumed/reformatted by that extension, affecting wiki footer/page output.

reproductionPaths.explanation: A Gitea wiki _Footer (or other wiki page) whose Markdown starts with '---' renders without the horizontal rule, and its blank-line-separated paragraphs run together on one line. The leading '---' is treated as the start of front matter instead of a rule. Without the leading '---' the same content renders normally.

sourceBugs.name: Wiki content that starts with a --- horizontal rule loses its paragraphs and the rule

reproductionPaths.expected: A '---' line renders as a horizontal rule and blank-line-separated blocks render as separate paragraphs, wherever the rule appears in the wiki content.
reproductionPaths.actual: A _Footer saved as '---', blank line, '**Special Footer QA**', blank line, 'FOOTER-SPECIAL-2026', blank line, a link, displayed below pages as one line ('Special Footer QA FOOTER-SPECIAL-2026 Structured guide') with no horizontal rule. The saved source still had the rule and blank lines; bold and the link still rendered.
reproSteps: In a repository wiki, create or edit _Footer.
Set its content to '---', a blank line, '**Footer title**', a blank line, 'Second paragraph', a blank line, and a link to another wiki page.
Save and open any wiki page.
Check whether the footer shows a horizontal rule and separate paragraphs.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea’s Markdown editor's Insert Table panel, an out-of-range size is clamped without telling the user: entering 0 Rows inserts a table with one row, and nothing indicates the value was changed.

rootCause.explanation: The insert handler applies Math.max(1,Math.min(100,rows/cols)) without reporting an input error or visibly correcting the form before insertion.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea’s Markdown editor's Insert Table panel, an out-of-range size is clamped without telling the user: entering 0 Rows inserts a table with one row, and nothing indicates the value was changed.

sourceBugs.name: Markdown table insertion silently turns Rows 0 into a one-row table

reproductionPaths.expected: When Rows is outside the allowed range, the editor tells the user (or refuses the value) instead of silently inserting a table of a different size.
reproductionPaths.actual: With Rows set to 0, Insert Table added a table with a header, separator and one Cell row, and no warning or adjustment message appeared; the one-row table stayed after saving and reopening.
reproSteps: Open the editor for a new wiki page.
Open the toolbar's Insert Table panel and set Rows to 0.
Insert the table.
Check whether the inserted table has a row and whether any message said Rows was changed.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, when a wiki (repository documentation) page's content starts with blank lines, opening it in the editor shows one fewer leading blank line than was saved, so saving it again without changes removes a blank line each time. The stored page keeps them; the editor loses one when loading.

rootCause.explanation: The shared editor template writes TextareaContent immediately after the textarea opening tag. HTML parsing discards one initial LF in a textarea, so a body beginning with a blank line loses one line when loaded and resaved.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, when a wiki page's content starts with blank lines, opening it in the editor shows one fewer leading blank line than was saved, so saving it again without changes removes a blank line each time. The stored page keeps them; the editor loses one when loading.

sourceBugs.name: Reopening a wiki page in the editor drops one leading blank line

reproductionPaths.expected: Opening a saved wiki page for editing shows its content exactly as saved, including all leading blank lines.
reproductionPaths.actual: A page saved with two blank lines before its text reopened in the editor with only one; saving again kept only one.
reproSteps: Create or edit a wiki page so its content starts with two blank lines followed by text, and save.
Open the page's Edit form again.
Count the blank lines before the text in the editor.

logicalBugs.explanation: On a Gitea wiki documentation page with headings far apart, edit the #fragment portion of the address in the same tab to target another heading. The address changes, but the page does not scroll to that heading; both ordinary and non-ASCII heading names are affected. Clicking an in-page link or opening the complete address in a new tab works, so those different navigation paths are outside this failure.

rootCause.explanation: web_src/js/markup/anchors.ts scrolls to a heading only on page load and on clicks of in-page links, adding the 'user-content-' prefix that rendered heading ids carry. There is no hashchange handler, and the browser cannot find the unprefixed fragment itself.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, on a rendered wiki page, editing the URL fragment in the address bar to another heading's anchor changes the URL but leaves the view where it was. This happens for ASCII and Unicode headings alike.

sourceBugs.name: Changing a wiki page's URL fragment in the same tab doesn't scroll to the heading

reproductionPaths.expected: Navigating to a heading fragment on the page already open scrolls that heading into view, as opening the same URL fresh does.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390×844 with the page open at #ascii-target, changing the address bar to the '日本語 café & punctuation!' heading's fragment left 'ASCII target' at the top. Going the other way, from the Unicode fragment to #ascii-target, also left the view unchanged. Opening either URL in a new tab, or clicking an in-page link, scrolls correctly.
reproSteps: Create a long wiki page with headings '## ASCII target' and '## 日本語 café & punctuation!' separated by enough text to scroll.
Open the page with #ascii-target appended and confirm ASCII target is at the top.
In the same tab, change the fragment in the address bar to the other heading's anchor and press Enter.
Observe the URL changes but the page does not scroll.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only same-tab fragment changes that are not link clicks, such as editing the address bar or setting location.hash. Not specific to Unicode headings; a report attributing it to Unicode matches if the trigger is a same-tab fragment change. Reports that clicking an in-page link, or loading or reloading a URL with a fragment, fails to scroll are the known-invalid entries.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea’s simple Markdown editor, inserting a table with the toolbar's Add table button puts the table template in the text, but Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) leaves it in place. Undo works for typed text and for the Bold button.

rootCause.explanation: web_src/js/features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts textareaInsertText inserts by assigning textarea.value, which clears the browser's native undo history, whereas the Bold button (@github/markdown-toolbar-element) inserts through the browser's editing commands and stays undoable.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea’s simple Markdown editor, inserting a table with the toolbar's Add table button puts the table template in the text, but Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) leaves it in place. Undo works for typed text and for the Bold button.

sourceBugs.name: Undo doesn't remove a table inserted from the Markdown editor toolbar

reproductionPaths.expected: Undo right after inserting a table removes the inserted table, like undo after other toolbar formatting.
reproductionPaths.actual: On a wiki page editor with 'intro ' typed, Add table > Add inserted a 3×3 table template; pressing Ctrl+Z left the table in the textarea. With 'hello world' and 'world' selected, the Bold button produced 'hello **world**' and Ctrl+Z restored 'hello world'.
reproSteps: Open a wiki page editor in the default (simple textarea) Markdown editor.
Type some text, then click the Add table toolbar button and insert the default 3×3 table.
Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) in the textarea and observe the table remains.

relatedReference.distinction: Both are the Markdown editor's table insertion. That entry is Rows 0 silently becoming one row; this entry is the inserted table not being undoable.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea, at phone width, the Delete Page confirmation for a wiki (repository documentation) page with a long title is pushed past the right edge, clipping the page name and the Yes button. Scrolling sideways reveals Yes but clips the dialog's left side.

rootCause.explanation: The delete modal interpolates the entire wiki title into an ordinary paragraph without a wiki-specific break or width constraint. A long unbroken title can impose an intrinsic width beyond the phone viewport; the exact modal centering/overflow contribution has not been independently reproduced here.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea, at phone width, the Delete Page confirmation for a wiki page with a long title is pushed past the right edge, clipping the page name and the Yes button. Scrolling sideways reveals Yes but clips the dialog's left side.

sourceBugs.name: Delete Page confirmation for a long wiki title runs off the mobile screen

reproductionPaths.expected: The deletion confirmation, the page name and both buttons fit within the mobile viewport.
reproductionPaths.actual: At 390px, on a page titled RESP-Stress-Long-title-with-many-headings-wide-table-and-long-code-content, Delete Page opened a dialog starting about 93px from the left and extending past the right edge. The Yes label and part of the page name were cut off; scrolling sideways showed the right side while clipping the left.
reproSteps: Create a wiki page with a long hyphenated title such as RESP-Stress-Long-title-with-many-headings-wide-table-and-long-code-content.
At a 390px-wide viewport, open the page and click Delete Page.
Observe the confirmation is clipped on the right; scroll sideways to reach Yes.

relatedReference.distinction: Same long-title mobile overflow. That entry is the closed 'Page:' selector on the page; this entry is the Delete Page confirmation dialog.

logicalBugs.explanation: In Gitea’s wiki (repository documentation) editor, a blank save from Write shows 'Please fill out this field.' If the user then switches to Preview and clicks Save Page again, nothing happens: no message and no navigation, so the user isn't told why the page won't save.

rootCause.explanation: web_src/js/features/comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts validateTextareaNonEmpty sets textarea.required = true when the blank textarea is visible and never clears it. In Preview the textarea is hidden, so the browser's native required check blocks the submit silently (a hidden control cannot show its bubble) before the submit handler in web_src/js/features/repo-wiki.ts can run and show the 'Require non-empty content' toast.

reproductionPaths.explanation: In Gitea’s wiki editor, a blank save from Write shows 'Please fill out this field.' If the user then switches to Preview and clicks Save Page again, nothing happens: no message and no navigation, so the user isn't told why the page won't save.

sourceBugs.name: Saving blank wiki content from Preview does nothing after an earlier blank save from Write

reproductionPaths.expected: A blank save from Preview explains that content is required, for example with the 'Require non-empty content' alert Gitea shows from Preview when no Write save was attempted first.
reproductionPaths.actual: On a new wiki page with a title and empty content, Save Page in Write showed 'Please fill out this field.' After switching to Preview, Save Page produced no message, no alert and no navigation. Without the earlier Write attempt, the same Preview save shows a red 'Require non-empty content' alert.
reproSteps: Open New Page in a wiki, enter a title and leave the content empty (or clear an existing page's content).
Click Save Page in the Write tab and see 'Please fill out this field.'
Switch to the Preview tab and click Save Page.
Observe that nothing happens and no message explains why.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reports that a blank Save Page from Preview gives no feedback match this entry, including ones that don't mention the earlier Write save.

sourceContext.validation: Static source analysis and clustering of existing reports; no new browser reproductions performed.
